event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CMCSA’s 2021-02-04 filing contains extensive, concrete disclosures that COVID-19 is both an already-realised and a continuing, material threat to virtually every line of business.  The text makes repeated, specific references to theme-park closures, disruptions to sports and film production, shifts to remote work, reduced advertising demand, liquidity concerns, bad-debt risk, and dependence on uncertain government restrictions and vaccine roll-outs.  Most statements describe impacts that have already reduced 2020 revenue and EBITDA; many also warn that negative effects will persist "near to medium term."  Because the pandemic was declared less than one year before the filing date, the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  The narrative is largely aggravating ("material adverse effect," "most significant impact"), with only limited mitigants (e.g., Cable results “were strong”).  Overall, the risk level is high and immediate, warranting elevated micro-scores in the 6-10 range for the clearest, company-wide impacts, and mid-range scores for narrower or partially mitigated statements.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has had, and will likely continue to have, a material adverse effect on our businesses and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly states past and future material adverse effect.
Applies broadly to "our businesses" and financial results.
Forward-looking persistence of risk ("will likely continue").

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, company-wide statement of both realised and continuing material harm merits a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 had material negative impacts on NBCUniversal and Sky results of operations during 2020.

components.reason: Confirms actual material negative impacts already realised.
Covers two major business segments, magnifying breadth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Segment-specific but still substantial realised harm earns a strong score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, in late February we temporarily closed our theme park in Japan, and in mid-March we temporarily closed our theme parks in Orlando and Hollywood, and although our parks in Orlando and Japan reopened with limited capacity in June 2020, our park in Hollywood remains closed.

components.reason: Details specific operational shutdowns across multiple geographies.
Notes continued closure of Hollywood park, indicating ongoing impact.
Partial reopening with limited capacity is a mitigating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete closure data shows direct revenue loss; limited reopening tempers but does not eliminate risk, yielding a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We expect the results of operations at our theme parks will continue to be negatively impacted in the near to medium term.

components.reason: Forecasts continuing negative impact—not merely historic.
Specifies time horizon (near to medium term), heightening immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking negative outlook for a key segment scores a moderate 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The creation and availability of our film and television programming globally have been and will continue to be disrupted, including as a result of the postponement or cancellation of sporting events, theatrical closures and the suspension of entertainment content production.

components.reason: Describes both current and ongoing global production disruptions.
Lists multiple drivers (sporting events, theatrical closures), amplifying risk breadth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad, continuing disruption across content pipelines warrants a 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We expect the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic will continue to have a material adverse impact on our consolidated results of operations over the near to medium term, although the extent of such impact will depend on restrictive governmental measures, further deterioration of the global economy and widespread availability of vaccines.

components.reason: Projects ongoing material adverse impact at consolidated level.
Highlights dependency on external, uncertain factors (government measures, vaccines).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Company-wide forward-looking materiality plus uncertainty earns 6.

evidence_list.snippet: The deterioration of economic conditions and increased economic uncertainty resulting from COVID-19 have resulted in reduced demand for certain of our residential and business services and reduced spending from advertisers, which have had and, while we have seen some improvement over the course of 2020, likely will continue to have, negative impacts on our revenue over the near to medium term.

components.reason: Links pandemic to reduced customer demand and advertising spend—key revenue drivers.
States impacts both realised and expected to persist.
Mention of some improvement is a mitigating note.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Revenue erosion across segments with slight mitigation justifies a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, we believe there is increased risk associated with collections on our outstanding receivables, and we have incurred, and may continue to incur, increases in our bad debt expense.

components.reason: Identifies heightened credit/collection risk and actual cost increases.
Forward-looking continuation of higher bad-debt expense.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific financial risk to cash flows—moderate severity score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The temporary closure of all of our theme parks had the most significant impact on our revenue and Adjusted EBITDA for the year ended December 31, 2020 on a consolidated basis.

components.reason: Quantifies closure as the "most significant" consolidated impact.
Refers to actual past financial metric impairment (revenue and EBITDA).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Largest single hit to company performance merits a strong 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Direct-to-consumer revenue has been negatively impacted as a result of lower sports subscription revenue due to the disruption of professional sports seasons and future periods may be negatively impacted as a result of the reopening plans and the extent of reopening of our commercial customers.

components.reason: Shows specific revenue stream already hurt (sports subscriptions).
Projects further negative impact tied to uncertain reopenings.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete segment revenue loss plus forward risk gives a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 continues to result in uncertainty in the ultimate timing of when, or the extent to which, sporting events will occur in future periods; their broadcast is expected to impact the timing, and potentially the amount, of revenue and expense recognition.

components.reason: Highlights significant forecasting uncertainty affecting revenue recognition.
Connects uncertainty to both revenue and expense timing—accounting risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational and accounting uncertainty around sports schedules scores 5.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 may also have the effect of heightening many of the other risks set forth below.

components.reason: States pandemic is a risk multiplier across multiple domains.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic risk-multiplier statement with no quantification earns a low-moderate 2.
